comment: The gateway's wire contract, minus everything upstream publishes. The signed payload families — the connect pair (funduq-connect-provider / funduq-connect-funduq), kyok-call, cancel, view, resolve, the actor-chain form — and the two delivery envelopes (delivered-run, delivered-completion, model_dump(by_alias=True)) are vectored in docs/upstream-contract-vectors.json, vendored verbatim from upstream funduq's docs/contract-vectors.json at contract revision 16. Two payload families moved at that revision and a signer built against revision 7 is wrong about both: the resolve proof signs the paused run's outstanding ask ids instead of a timestamp ('funduq-resolve:{runId}:{sha256 of the ids, sorted and NUL-joined}') and rides the wire as {publicKey, signature} with no freshness window, while funduq-view is a new family for reading a chain-bound run ({publicKey, timestamp, signature}, 60s window). The funduq-delegate family is GONE — the session delegation certificate was removed at revision 15 and nothing here signs, sends or relays one. What remains this file's to state: the wire version, and each socket's frame vocabulary. All three in-repo implementations' suites (gateway, souk-agent-sdk, souk-client-sdk) plus the Go pod-probe consume this file; the inbound frame sets are the module constants the gateway's dispatch reads, asserted equal in tests.

handshake.comment: Two frames. The provider fetches {ticket, funduqPublicKey} from POST /tickets out of band, computes proof = sign(provider_connect_payload(funduqPublicKey, ticket, nonce)) BEFORE connecting, and opens with hello; funduq answers welcome, whose 'answer' is its signature over funduq_connect_payload(ticket, nonce) — the provider verifies it against the pinned key (confirm_connect / WrongFunduq) before treating the link as open. Refusals close 1008 with a reason; 1011 is reserved for server faults. The /ws/kyok hello carries no maxConcurrentRuns. Attach is NAMELESS: nothing is served until a register frame on the open link.

frames.comment: Frame types per socket, after the two-frame handshake. A run frame is {'type': 'run', **DeliveredRun} — dumped by_alias=True and NEVER exclude_none, because RunAgentInput has required fields that are legitimately null ('state', 'forwardedProps') and stripping them makes a good run come back as a permanent refusal; a completion request is {'type': 'completionRequest', 'requestId', **DeliveredCompletion} (actorChain included since contract revision 7), whose 'body' is validated as OpenAI's own chat-completion request shape — 'model' among the required fields — with extension keys allowed through verbatim, and a body that is not one is a 400 before the socket is touched. The ack is three-valued: accepted true, false (transient decline — the run stays queued), or false with a 'reason' (permanent refusal); an ack arriving after funduq's delivery window matches nothing and is simply dropped, which is a guard and not a path. Registration frames are unsigned — the link is the credential: register carries the FULL roster (a smaller batch withdraws omitted names), 'registered' echoes what is now live, deleteAgent/deleteModel remove one record ('deleted' confirms; a refusal — e.g. an agent with a conversation behind it — is answered with an 'error' frame and the socket stays open). The one query is thread_messages. Full field semantics in docs/server-mode.md.
frames.register_agent_entry_comment: One element of register.agents, and it IS funduq_contract.Registration — extra='forbid', so a misspelt key is a validation error at the door rather than a field silently dropped on the way into core. 'takesInterjections' arrived at contract revision 12: the remote link declares, per agent, whether that agent takes a run addressed at its thread's live run, derived by the SDK from the presence of the interjection hook and never typed by an author. funduq reads it back off the link at registration and writes it onto the agent card as the interjection extension's URI. An entry omitting it behaves exactly as before.
